PROCEDURAL BACKGROUND
On March 16, 2026, after completing mediation, the Redwood City School
District (District) filed a request for factfinding pursuant to the Educational Employment
Relations Act (EERA)1 with the Public Employment Relations Board (PERB) regarding
its negotiations with the California School Employees Association and its Chapter 5
(CSEA) regarding the reduction of hours of Library Media Technical Associate (LMTA)
and Library Media Assistant (LMA) positions at the District’s school library sites.2
On March 16 and 18, 2026, the parties selected their factfinding panel
members and on April 20, 2026, PERB notified the undersigned arbitrator that he had
been selected as the Chair of the factfinding panel.
On May 6, 2026,3 the Chair held an organizational meeting where the agenda
of the factfinding proceeding, factfinding proceeding dates, options for closing
arguments, and the issuance date of the factfinding report and recommendation(s) for
settlement (factfinding report) were discussed. The parties agreed that the factfinding

hours of LMTAs/LMAs: Adelante Selby School, Garfield School, Hoover School,
Roy Cloud School, Clifford School and McKinley Institute of Technology/North Star
Academy (MIT/North Star).

proceeding would be scheduled for May 19 and 20, 2026; the parties would be
submitting oral closing arguments on May 20, 2026; and the factfinding report would
be issued on June 3, 2026.
The factfinding proceeding was held and concluded on May 19 and 20, 2026.
Both parties presented arguments/exhibits surrounding the issues in dispute. Both
parties made closing arguments at the end of their cases-in-chief rather than at the
end of both parties’ presentations. On May 22, 2026, the Chair asked the parties for
the District’s job descriptions for both the LMTA and the LMA positions and the
District’s Fiscal Stabilization Plan mentioned in one of the slides of its presentation.
Neither party objected to the documents being provided to the Chair and the panel
and the District provided these documents to the entire panel and CSEA.
STATEMENT OF THE ISSUE
The parties were able to jointly stipulate to the issue in this matter which was:
Should the weekly hours (and resulting full-time equivalency – FTE) of
certain classified Library Media Assistants and Library Media [Technical]
Associates be reduced?
FACTFINDING CRITERIA
EERA provides statutory criteria in Government Code section 3548.2,
subd. (b)(1) through (7), for the factfinding panel to consider, weigh, and be guided by
in determining findings and recommendations. Those statutory criteria are:
“(b) In arriving at their findings and recommendations, the factfinders
shall consider, weigh, and be guided by all the following criteria:
“(1) State and federal laws that are applicable to the employer.
“(2) Stipulations of the parties.
3

“(3) The interests and welfare of the public and the financial
ability of the public school employer.
“(4) Comparison of the wages, hours, and conditions of
employment of the employees involved in the factfinding
proceeding with the wages, hours, and conditions of
employment of other employees performing similar services
and with other employees generally in public school
employment in comparable communities.
“(5) The consumer price index for goods and services,
commonly known as the cost of living.
“(6) The overall compensation presently received by the
employees, including direct wage compensation, vacations,
holidays, and other excused time, insurance and pensions,
medical and hospitalization benefits; the continuity and stability
of employment; and all other benefits received.
“(7) Any other facts, not confined to those specified in
paragraphs (1) to (6), inclusive, which are normally or
traditionally taken into consideration in making the findings and
recommendations.
Of these factfinding factors, the parties agreed that the statutory criteria listed in
Government Code section 3548.2, subd. (b)(4), was inapplicable to this factfinding
proceeding.
FINDINGS OF FACT
Stipulations of Uncontested Facts between the Parties
The parties agreed to the following pertinent uncontested facts in this matter:
“1. [The District] is a public school employer within the meaning of
Government Code section 3540.1(k) of [EERA].
“2. CSEA and its Redwood City Chapter [5] is a recognized employee
organization within the meaning of Government Code
4

section 3540.1(1) of [EERA] and has been duly recognized as the
representative of the classified non-management bargaining unit[.]
“3. The parties have complied with [EERA] with regard to the selection
of the Factfinding Panel and have met or waived the statutory time
limitations applicable to this proceeding.
“4. The District has complied with section 5.1.4 of the parties’ collective
bargaining agreement which provides:
“When the District needs to increase or decrease the hours of a
bargaining unit position it should provide written notice and an
opportunity to bargain to CSEA.”
Background
The District is a public school employer which educates students from
prekindergarten through the eighth grade. Generally, the individual schools within the
-
Districts employ LMTAs and LMAs who provide library media services to the students
attending those schools within the District. Usually, a singular LMTA or an LMA is
assigned to an individual school site library and reports to the district librarian and the
school site principal:
The job description for LMTA provides in pertinent part:
“REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES
“[ . . . ]
“1. Assist with the training and professional development of school
library media assistants, particularly in the areas of new and/or
upgrades of software programs such as . . . which are necessary for
the smooth functioning of Redwood City School District's Library
Media Centers. This will include attending training sessions with
the technology department and organizing and presenting
workshops for [LMAs] in newly adopted software programs.
5

“2. Provide troubleshooting services for software and equipment and
initiate help tickets for equipment that needs to be repaired by the
Technology Department.
“3. Communicate to [LMAs] various methods and techniques used for
machine readable cataloging [(MARC)], MARC records, budget
monitoring using Excel, library program activities, lesson planning,
and presentations using PowerPoint or overheads.
“4. Serve as a mentor to a designated group of [LMAs].
“5. Provide exemplary library media service and programming in the
following areas:
“● Organize and maintain the routine operation of a school library
media center including maintenance and weeding of the
collection; receive, process, circulate and shelve print and
non-print materials according to accepted library procedures.
“● Assist teachers in teaching students basic information literacy
skills; i.e., access, use and evaluate print and non-print
materials to improve literacy.
“● Assist students and teachers in locating and selecting
appropriate materials; assist students with special class theme
projects or conduct story time as required.
“● Maintain routine records related to library activities including
circulation of books, monies collected and lost materials.
“● Schedule library media times for classes. Train, assign and
monitor work of volunteer and student helpers.
“● Maintain the library media center in a clean and orderly
condition providing an environment conducive to learning and
literacy; assist in maintaining the discipline of students.
6

“● Create displays to promote reading and library media units and
themes.
(Bolding included in quotation.)
The job description for the LMA provides in pertinent part:
“REPRESENTATIVE DUTIES:
“Organize and maintain the routine operation of a school library media
center including maintenance and weeding of the collection; receive,
process, circulate and shelve print and non-print materials according to
magnet theme.
“Assist teachers in teaching students basic information literacy skills; i.e.:
access, use and evaluate print and non-print materials to improve
literacy through the magnet theme.
“Assist students and teachers in locating and selecting appropriate
materials; assist students with special class magnet theme projects or
conduct story time as required.
“Maintain routine records related to library activities including circulation
of books, monies collected and lost materials.
“Schedule library media times for classes. Train, assign and monitor
work of volunteer and student helpers.
“Maintain the library media center in a clean and orderly condition
providing an environment conducive to learning and literacy; assist in
maintaining the discipline of students.
“Create displays to promote reading and library media units and magnet
theme.”
(Bolding included in quotation.)
A full-time equivalent LMTA/LMA is scheduled to work 37.5 hours per week.
The 37.5-hour week includes 2.5 hours in paid breaks a week (two 15-minute breaks
7

per day) and a half-hour daily unpaid lunch period.4 In general, the school site
libraries have schedules in which individual grade classes come to their libraries for
half-hour periods—usually from Monday to Wednesday and Friday. Thursday is
usually a day when the LMTAs and LMAs meet with each other and the district
librarian once a month for a limited period of time. Thursday is also the workday on
which LMTAs/LMAs complete their assigned tasks which do not involve hosting a
class of students in the school site library.5
The hours of operation of the library at the six remaining school library sites
varied, even if the LMTA/LMA was scheduled to work 37.5 hours a week. The
Adelante Selby School library operated from 7:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. The Hoover and
Clifford School libraries operated from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The Roy Cloud School
library operated from 8:00 a.m. to 2:45 p.m. The Garfield School library operated from
8:10 a.m. to 3:45 p.m. Lastly, the MIT/North Star Library operated from 8:30 a.m. to
4:00 p.m.6
At the District, LMTAs are compensated at pay grade 25.5 ($35.25 to $44.94 an
hour) while LMAs are compensated at pay grade 19.5 ($26.23 to $33.56 an hour).
4 Some LMTAs and LMAs work less than 37.5 hours a week.

a reduction in hours could not be achieved, one site (the Hoover School library)
hosted student classes on Thursdays, but the general practice according to the school
site library schedules was that the LMTAs and LMAs used Thursday to perform their
duties which did not involve hosting a class of students or the preparation involved
with hosting that class.
6 MIT/North Star shared the same library. The LMTA/LMA who worked at the
MIT/North Star library worked 35 hours a week.
8

The primary difference between the two classifications, LMTA and LMA, is that the
LMTA position requires the completion of a Library Media Technology certificate or the
completion of a library media program accredited from a college, which then required
the LMTA to complete additional duties.
Declining Enrollment
The District has experienced a continuing trend of declining student enrollment
over the last ten school years. From school year 2015-20167 to 2024-2025, student
enrollment at the District has declined from 8,414 to 6,409 students8—a decline of
2,005 students, or a 24 percent reduction in students. In school year 2018-2019, the
District had to close four of its schools due to declining student enrollment.
Fiscal Stabilization Plan
On December 11, 2024, the Superintendent recommended for approval to the
District Board a Budget Renewal Initiative which proposed to save the District
$6.6 million dollars to address the expiration of one-time federal and state pandemic
relief funds and ensure the District’s long-term financial stability.9 The cost-saving
proposals which the Superintendent recommended to the District Board included:

determined its staffing and weekly hour allotment of LMTAs/LMAs to individual school
sites. On March 7, 2016, the District and CSEA agreed to an increased allotment of
hours for LMTAs/LMAs at various individual school sites.
8 Unfortunately for the District, its current student enrollment and
projected student enrollment continue to decline. The District student enrollment
for school year 2025-2026 was 6,309 students and the anticipated District student
enrollment for school year 2026-2027 is 6,100 students.
9 This initiative later became known as the Fiscal Stabilization Plan.
9

(1) reducing seven district and school site administrator positions; (2) reducing five
district office positions; (3) reducing funding to specific school sites; (4) reducing the
hours of LMTAs/LMAs at nine schools and increasing the hours of LMTAs/LMAs at
two schools due to the overall declining student enrollment; (5) reducing the hours of
13 paraeducators and eliminating two contracted positions within the District’s Special
Education Department.
The District Board agenda item for Proposal 4 regarding the reduction/increase
of LMTAs/LMAs hours at eleven school library sites provided:
“Superintendent Recommendation #4: Adjust Staffing Due to
Ongoing Declining Enrollment
“Proposal: Address staffing due to projected enrollment fluctuations for
2025-[2026], for a savings of approximately $200,000
“● Adjust hours for [LMTAs] at nine schools (reductions) and two schools
(increases).
“● Reduce office staff hours
“● Conduct an analysis of classroom staffing needs.
“Rationale: Although [transitional kindergarten] expansion has stabilized overall
districtwide enrollment numbers during the last three school years, we continue
to see families with students in all grade levels leaving the Bay Area and the
state. While the community disagreed with reductions related to enrollment
(56 [percent] to 44 [percent]), district demographers continue to study our area,
which shows an ongoing decline each year with approximately 1,000 fewer
students by 2033-[2034].”
(Bolding and underlining included in quotation.)
Notice to Bargain Reduction in Hours of LMTAs/LMAs
On March 12, 2025, the District provided CSEA with notice that it intended to
reduce the hours of the LMTA and LMA positions due to the District’s lack of funds
and lack of work resulting from declining student reenrollment.. The notice included a
10

spreadsheet which indicated the proposed reduction in weekly hours to the specific
LMTA/LMA positions at specific school site libraries and stated that the reductions
were to take effect at the beginning of the 2025-2026 school year. The parties
bargained regarding these proposed changes to LMTAs/LMAs weekly hours at the
eleven school library sites. The parties were able to come to agreements as to a
reduction/increase in weekly hours at five of the eleven school library sites.
Reduction in Work and Final Bargaining Proposals
The District’s contention that the LMTAs/LMAs had less work to perform is
based upon the extraneous preparation time which LMTAs/LMAs had in their weekly
schedules. In a sense, in attempting to right-size the hours of the LMTAs/LMAs, the
District focused on the essential duties of LMTAs/LMAs as to (1) the amount of
individual class student time (half-hour increment classes) which came to a school
library site a week, (2) half-hour preparatory periods for each half-hour increment of
individual class time, (3) lunch periods where the LMTA/LMA hosted students, and
(4) additional LMTA/LMA preparation time allotted to the library’s program design (the
Thursday workday where LMTAs/LMAs completed their assignments set forth in their
job descriptions which were not related to students being presence.)

In addition to the District’s proposal regarding its hourly reductions to the
LMTAs/LMAs weekly schedules, it proposed an effective date of January 1, 2026 for
the implementation of this reduction. Additionally, the District proposed that all of the
LMTAs/LMAs at these six individual school sites would continue to receive full-time
equivalent employee health insurance benefits as long as the employee remained in
their assigned LMTA/LMA position at their school library site.
CSEA argues that its last proposal still saves the District $83,828.00 while the
District’s proposals save the District $142,952.00. The difference in cost savings
between the two proposals was $59,124.00. In reviewing the District’s unrestricted
general fund budget reserves in the 2025-2026 school year Second Interim Financial
Report,12 CSEA contends that the District has the financial ability to pay this
differential of cost savings as the District has $11,563,122.21 in cash reserves.
Deep Hourly Reductions to Incumbent LMTAs/LMAs and the Consumer Price Index
CSEA contends that the District’s September 17, 2025 last, best and final
proposal imposes deep hourly reductions to LMTAs/LMAs which create significant
financial hardships for the LMTAs/LMAs. The LMTAs/LMAs at Garfield School,
Adelante Selby School and MIT/North Start will experience a reduction in hours at
37 percent, 20 percent and 18 percent, respectively. On top of these reductions,
these same employees will lose an additional 3.8 percent of purchasing power as a
result of the consumer price index (CPI). (See Western Region CPI for April 2026.)
12 This Second Interim Financial Report sets forth the actual revenues and
expenditures of the District up to January 31, 2026.

CSEA asserts that such deep reductions will only result in future negative implications
as to the recruitment and retention of LMTAs/LMAs for the District.
APPLICATION OF STATUTORY CRITERIA AND RECOMMENDATIONS
Unlike interest arbitration, where a third-party neutral sets the terms of a
new agreement, a third-party neutral in an EERA factfinding report simply provides
recommendation(s) as to terms for settlement, which shall be advisory only.
(Gov. Code, § 3548.3, subd. (a).) In essence, the impasse resolution procedure,
which includes the factfinding process, is a continuation of the collective bargaining
process. (Regents of the University of California (2026) PERB Decision No. 3010-H,
p. 5; San Bernardino County Superintendent of Schools (2024) PERB Decision
No. 2934, p. 16.) Ultimately, the parties must persuade one another of their positions,
and the neutral factfinder simply provides an outside perspective to assist the parties
to possibly come to an agreement over matters within the scope of representation.
(Government Code section 3548; City of Oakland (2018) PERB Order No. Ad-462-M,
p. 4; County of Ventura (2018) PERB Order No. Ad-461-M, p. 5.) Both parties to the
factfinding process are statutorily obligated to participate in this process in good faith.
(Regents of the University of California, supra, p. 6; San Bernardino County
Superintendent of Schools, supra, p. 16.)
Reduction in Hours of the LMTAs/LMAs at the Six Remaining School Library Sites
The District finds itself in an ongoing fiscal dilemma of having to face the
continuing reality of significant declining student enrollment from over a decade, into
the 2026-2027 school year, and beyond (to the 2033-2034 school year). The District
has instituted a fiscal stabilization plan in order to provide stability for the District given
14

the loss of federal and state pandemic relief funds that were expiring and in order to
provide fiscal stability for the District. It has made reductions in other areas besides
library services to achieve this goal.
While the District has decided to eliminate other positions in other
classifications, it has decided instead to reduce the hours of LMTAs/LMAs in order
that the District may provide the appropriate level of library media services to its
students at its individual school library sites. The District measured the duties of its
LMTAs/LMAs based upon the present need of the individual classes which
LMTAs/LMAs host and the preparation time associated with hosting these individual
classes; the hosting of lunch/recess periods for students; and the other duties within
the LMTA/LMA job descriptions not related to the hosting of individual classes which
were to be performed on Thursdays. This focused targeting of LMTA/LMA duties was
reasonable and logical to the primary mission of the District’s education of its students.
The numbers of reduced hours per week based upon these core duties fall closer to
the numbers of reduced hours per week set forth in the District’s proposals than
CSEA’s proposals.
CSEA asserts that some of the hourly reductions of LMTAs/LMAs are too
severe and will lead to future recruitment and retention issues and that the District
possesses an adequate amount of unrestricted cash reserves which provide the
District with the ability to absorb the cost of a smaller reduction in hours similar to
CSEA’s proposal. This argument carries some weight, especially as to the 37 percent
reduction in hours proposed upon the LMTA/LMA employed at Garfield School, and
the Chair agrees that such a reduction in hours to that position will cause
15

recruitment/retention problems in the future. However, as the decline of student
enrollment has not been forecasted to reverse nor even plateau, CSEA’s argument
ultimately loses its force. Unfortunately for both the District and CSEA, the decline of
student enrollment will continue. As such, it is in the interests and welfare of the
public and the financial ability of the public school employer that the hourly reductions
in the LMTAs/LMAs’ workweek as proposed by the District be accepted, with a
modification as to implementation of the effective date of the reduction in hours being
postponed to the beginning of the upcoming 2026-2027 school year.
Recommendation(s) for Settlement: Pursuant to Government Code
section 3548.2, subdivision (b)(3), the Chair recommends that the District’s proposal
as to the reduction in hours of the LMTAs/LMAs as to the six remaining individual
library sites, including its augmented health benefits proposal, be accepted by the
parties. The effective date of the reduction of hours, however, should start at the
beginning of the 2026-2027 school year as the LMTAs/LMAs have already worked the
hours scheduled for them in the 2025-2026 school year.
In addition to such recommendation, it is also recommended that by the end of
fall semester of the 2026-2027 school year, that the District conduct an evaluation as
to the adequacy of the allotment of the reduced weekly hours of the LMTAs/LMAs as
to the six remaining school library sites in order to determine whether the
LMTAs/LMAs are able to complete the duties set forth in their job descriptions within
the reduced allotment of weekly hours. Such evaluation shall include seeking input
from CSEA and the unit employee affected by the weekly reduction in hours.
16

DISSENT OF EMPLOYEE ORGANIZATION PANEL MEMBER
I respectfully dissent from the Chair's recommendation that the District's proposal regarding the
reduction of hours for the remaining Library Media Technical Associate (“LMTA”) and Library
Media Assistant (“LMA”) positions be adopted.
The record establishes that the District faces legitimate fiscal challenges arising from declining
enrollment and the expiration of one-time funding sources. However, the evidence does not
demonstrate that the magnitude of the proposed reductions is necessary or that the District's
staffing analysis fully accounts for the scope of duties performed by LMTAs and LMAs.
The District's rationale is based primarily upon scheduled student contact time, associated
preparation periods, and designated work periods. Yet the job descriptions for both
classifications include numerous responsibilities that are not directly tied to classroom
scheduling, including collection maintenance, circulation management, literacy support,
assistance to students and staff, supervision of volunteers, development of library programming,
and other operational functions essential to the effective operation of school libraries. The record
does not persuasively establish that these duties can be adequately performed within the
substantially reduced hours proposed by the District.
Moreover, the proposed reductions would have a significant adverse impact on affected
employees, particularly at Garfield School where the reductions are especially severe. The Chair
expressly recognizes the likelihood that at least some of these reductions may create recruitment
and retention concerns. This consideration weighs against adopting the District's proposal in its
entirety.
Further evidence demonstrates that CSEA's final proposal would still produce meaningful and
ongoing cost savings while reducing the adverse effects on bargaining unit employees and
preserving a greater level of library services for students. In light of the District's acknowledged
reserve levels and the relatively limited fiscal difference between the parties' positions, a less
drastic reduction in hours better balances the District's financial interests with the interests of
employees and the educational needs of the District's students.
For these reasons, I would reject the District's proposed reductions and recommend adoption of a
modified staffing plan more closely aligned with CSEA's final proposal, together with a
subsequent evaluation of workload and service delivery during the 2026-2027 school year.
Accordingly, I dissent.
Dated: June 2, 2026
Nathan Jennings, Senior Labor Relations Representative
